newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds suffered from investors' indecision which kept activity thin and nervous.
The December Confederate bond futures contract was near day's lows at the close, after dropping early in the session.
"It was a quiet market. Investors are watching the market and are not active. Traders are waiting for any news that could offer the market direction," one trader said.

Prices may also have been pressured after the Swiss franc fell to its lowest levels against the mark since mid-July, with the mark rising to 82.60 Swiss centimes. Swiss bonds were also undermined by a softer tone in German Bund futures.
Traders noted that in the meantime, investors also appeared to be switching into Italian lira bonds and out of Bunds, a factor which may have further eroded the Swiss market.
Volume in Confederate bond futures was a low 2,237 contracts, one dealer said. But he added that volume was up compared with the previous two sessions.
The Swiss National Bank released money supply data early in the day, which showed money supply in September still above the SNB's medium-term target of one percent growth per annum.
But economists said that growth in September had slowed from August and did not appear to pose any inflation threat.
Traders said a key focus was likely to be U.S. employment data due next week on Friday.
Traders were also seen squaring positions before U.S. durable goods data due tomorrow.
"We had a little bit of a tricky week, traders don't feel comfortable with the market ahead of the figures and are taking a break. Most of the market is long," one trader said.
New issuance has been dampened by market uncertainty.
A 10-year domestic 500 million Swiss franc issue for the Swiss Pfandbriefzentrale set Wednesday was quoted at 4.09 percent by lead manager Zuricher Kantonalbank.
According to the lead the issue traded as high as 4.07 percent yield on Wednesday at minus 0.40.
It was quoted at minus 0.75/0.55 on the 100-7/8 issue price on Thursday.
